actual_scope: Four laws of the t = -1 per-port contract (M = [[1,-1],[1,0]], X = x - y, Y = x) on P104, each with an exact self-contained check: (1) the charge law and the corrected anchored deficiency law of the relay family, with Y-atom counting; (2) the carried-row law: one owned MOVE lowers the V-span deficiency by at most 1; (3) multi-hub additivity: per-hub deficiencies telescope to dim K = 96 on E8/P104; (4) the per-J odd unit of the t = -1 native, its lift and gauge ledger, and its invariance under sigma-fixed automorphisms. Y-atom conservation is stated as conditional on Lemma A.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a constructive helper-basis or causal-split improvement. This package instead states and checks laws that bound the t = -1 contract on P104; it makes no kappa claim.
bottleneck_link: Each law prices a class of t = -1 designs: the owned bill of the relay family (laws 1-2), any multi-hub settlement (law 3), and any attempt to remove the per-J odd unit by gauge, automorphism or finite order (law 4).

open_questions.question: Is Lemma A (premise PA: a y-atom of column q leaves only during Y_q's neutral period or through an owned copy) true for arbitrary legal programs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only unproved step of Y-atom conservation D >= n - r - N_neutral - N_owned, which bounds every t = -1 owned bill on P104 (96 per call with N = 0).
open_questions.first_step: State a content-class invariant for public ADD sequences and test it on A3/A4 programs with courier and twin operations.

open_questions.question: Can an L-side network deliver all of a column's L-side charge after Y_t passes its partner line (the Y-prefix schedule) at a public cost below the U-side relay floor?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Per-cell anchored re-adds remove the owned bill exactly (D = 0 on E8 matchings); the remaining cost of that schedule sits entirely on the L side.
open_questions.first_step: On the A3 toy, find frames where the Y-prefix L-side gives and receives are legal, and compute D and the public bill.
